summary: Fresh-session audit of the captured omnipaxos snapshot (crate 0.2.3, commit 827f304); read the core decision/authority paths (sequence_paxos mod/leader/follower, internal_storage, state_cache, omni_paxos) and registered one sourced question plus a deterministic two-case in-process harness being submitted for execution. Question: after a replica has already accepted its configuration's StopSign, does re-synchronizing it (PrepareReq->Prepare->Promise->AcceptSync, reached by the public reconnected() call) keep its reported accepted index within its log content, so the StopSign stays observable as decided and the decided log stays readable? Source reading says no: send_accsync hands the follower's accepted index (which already counts its stored StopSign) to create_log_sync as sync_idx, create_log_sync attaches the sender's StopSign unchanged, and sync_log adds that StopSign a second time, so the follower's accepted index ends one past its log; the follower then reports that inflated index in Accepted, and the leader's rule (accepted index above decided index plus a write quorum) would let it set a decided index past the entries it holds. The harness (draft/omnipaxos/tests/assurance_generated.rs, three real instances, MemoryStorage, deterministic FIFO queue, no snapshots, batch_size 1) samples the public endpoints before and after both followers call reconnected(3), with a control case that repeats the identical prefix without reconnecting, and emits one distinct event per lifecycle stage for the eight comparisons. Knowledge records only the source-located stop-sign index accounting as a behavior; the source-only interpretation is marked conditional with defect_claim unresolved, listing the counterevidence (the documented user flow expects a new instance once the StopSign is observed decided; the +1 is correct when the prefix does not yet contain the StopSign) and the limits. Validation passes and execution is requested. Incomplete: the execution result, confirmation or refutation of the inflation and of the leader-side phantom decision, the anchored requirement/declaration anchors dropped to satisfy the submission checker, and any second independent lead.
